title: Typed transport error record
description: One record per classified failure. R6 exists so that a transport failure is never stored as a model failure; that only holds if the taxonomy is exhaustive, so every exception on the send path must land on one of these categories (see UnknownTransportError) rather than propagating raw.

category.description: Pre-connection covers DNS, refused, and TLS failures -- the class a 'timeout' check would otherwise miss, leaving a network outage recorded as the model producing nothing. `request_rejected` exists because a 400 is not always a tool-schema problem: the captured 400s on this provider carry the same `type` and `code` for a bad model name, an orphaned tool result, and a dropped reasoning field, so the status alone cannot classify them and the catch-all for a rejected request must not be `unknown_transport` -- which is retryable, and retrying a request the provider will refuse again is a loop. `credential_missing` is the same argument one step earlier: the refusal happens on this side, before any I/O, and still needs a row (R3) and a category (R6).

billable.description: Whether the provider may have charged for this attempt. A declared default, not a measured fact: the only evidence of actual billing is the usage block on a call_terminal row.
